claim: FtsZ polymerizes into protofilaments, which further assemble into higher-order structures at future division sites to form the Z-ring.
source: The prokaryotic tubulin homolog FtsZ polymerizes into protofilaments, which further assemble into higher-order structures at future division sites to form the Z-ring, a dynamic structure essential for bacterial cell division.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about FtsZ assembly.

claim: The Z-ring is a dynamic structure essential for bacterial cell division.
source: The prokaryotic tubulin homolog FtsZ polymerizes into protofilaments, which further assemble into higher-order structures at future division sites to form the Z-ring, a dynamic structure essential for bacterial cell division.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about the Z-ring.

claim: Two crystallographic structures of a pair of FtsZ protofilaments were solved showing antiparallel assembly through two different inter-protofilament lateral interfaces.
source: In this study, we solved two crystallographic structures of a pair of FtsZ protofilaments, and demonstrated that they assemble in an antiparallel manner through the formation of two different inter-protofilament lateral interfaces.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract, supported by crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lateral interactions between FtsZ protofilaments occur in living cells.
source: Our in vivo photocrosslinking studies confirmed that such lateral interactions occur in living cells, and disruption of the lateral interactions rendered cells unable to divide.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo photocrosslinking experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Disruption of lateral interactions between FtsZ protofilaments renders cells unable to divide.
source: Our in vivo photocrosslinking studies confirmed that such lateral interactions occur in living cells, and disruption of the lateral interactions rendered cells unable to divide.
evidence: This is supported by complementation assays shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The inherently weak lateral interactions enable FtsZ protofilaments to self-organize into a dynamic Z-ring.
source: The inherently weak lateral interactions enable FtsZ protofilaments to self-organize into a dynamic Z-ring.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Z-ring serves as a scaffold to recruit other cell division proteins that collectively constitute the divisome.
source: Once formed, the Z-ring serves as a scaffold to recruit other cell division proteins that collectively constitute the divisome (Dajkovic and Lutkenhaus, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: During cell division, the Z-ring constricts at the leading edge of the invaginating septum, eventually causing a mother cell to divide into two daughter cells.
source: During cell division, the Z-ring constricts at the leading edge of the invaginating septum, eventually causing a mother cell to divide into two daughter cells (Bi and Lutkenhaus, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: FtsZ subunits interact through two putative sets of interfaces: longitudinal interfaces that join subunits head-to-tail to form protofilaments, and lateral interfaces that occur between protofilaments.
source: FtsZ subunits have been suggested to interact through two putative sets of interfaces, longitudinal interfaces that join the subunits in a head-to-tail manner thereby forming a protofilament, and lateral interfaces that occur between protofilaments.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: FtsZ subunits readily assemble into protofilaments in vitro.
source: FtsZ subunits readily assemble into protofilaments in vitro (Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Romberg et al., 2001), and crystal structures of FtsZ protofilaments have been determined for both straight (Matsui et al., 2012; Tan et al., 2012) and curved conformations (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Crystal structures of FtsZ protofilaments have been determined for both straight and curved conformations.
source: FtsZ subunits readily assemble into protofilaments in vitro (Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Romberg et al., 2001), and crystal structures of FtsZ protofilaments have been determined for both straight (Matsui et al., 2012; Tan et al., 2012) and curved conformations (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: In vitro, FtsZ protofilaments associate via lateral interfaces to form higher-order structures such as sheets.
source: In vitro, FtsZ protofilaments have been observed to further associate via lateral interfaces to form higher-order structures such as sheets (Bramhill and Thompson, 1994; Erickson et al., 1996; González et al., 2003; Löwe and Amos, 1999; Löwe and Amos, 2000; Oliva et al., 2003; Yu and Margolin, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Several studies strongly suggested that lateral interfaces across protofilaments are important for FtsZ function.
source: While several studies strongly suggested that lateral interfaces across protofilaments are important for FtsZ function (Dajkovic et al., 2008; Lan et al., 2009; Milam et al., 2012; Szwedziak et al., 2014), the precise nature and the functional relevance of these lateral interfaces remain largely unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The precise nature and functional relevance of lateral interfaces between FtsZ protofilaments remain largely unclear.
source: While several studies strongly suggested that lateral interfaces across protofilaments are important for FtsZ function (Dajkovic et al., 2008; Lan et al., 2009; Milam et al., 2012; Szwedziak et al., 2014), the precise nature and the functional relevance of these lateral interfaces remain largely unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: MtbFtsZ and EcFtsZ are able to form protofilament bundles in vitro in the presence of DEAE-dextran.
source: Our electron microscopy analysis showed that MtbFtsZ and FtsZ from Escherichia coli (EcFtsZ) are able to form protofilament bundles in vitro in the presence of DEAE-dextran (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy images shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: The ability of both EcFtsZ and MtbFtsZ protofilaments to form bundles suggests that the lateral interface of FtsZ protofilaments is a common and conserved characteristic.
source: The fact that protofilaments of both EcFtsZ and MtbFtsZ are able to form such assemblies, as observed previously (Erickson et al., 1996; Löwe and Amos, 1999), suggests that the lateral interface of FtsZ protofilaments is a common and conserved characteristic.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations and previous studies.

claim: A new hexagonal crystal structure of MtbFtsZ was determined to an Rfree factor of 27.3% at a resolution of 2.7 Å.
source: We have now identified candidates for these interfaces in a new hexagonal crystal of MtbFtsZ, which has been determined to an Rfree factor of 27.3% at a resolution of 2.7 Å (Materials and methods, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: The new MtbFtsZ structure is double-stranded and reveals curved filaments in an antiparallel arrangement.
source: Compared with our earlier MtbFtsZ structure (Li et al., 2013), our newly determined MtbFtsZ structure is similarly double-stranded and reveals curved filaments in an antiparallel arrangement.
evidence: This is based on the crystallographic structure determination.

claim: In the new MtbFtsZ structure, the inter-protofilament interface is located at the external faces of helices H3, H4, and H5 in the N-terminal subdomain (lateral interface 2).
source: However, in this new structure, the inter-protofilament interface is located at the external faces of helices H3, H4, and H5 in the N-terminal subdomain (lateral interface 2, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on the crystallographic structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In the previously identified lateral interface, Arg229 of one subunit and Asp301 of the other formed two pairs of salt bridges, burying a surface area of approximately 210 Å2.
source: In the previously identified lateral interface (Li et al., 2013), Arg229 of one subunit and Asp301 of the other formed two pairs of salt bridges, burying a surface area of approximately 210 Å2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the previous MtbFtsZ structure.

claim: The lateral interface in the new MtbFtsZ structure is composed of basic residues Arg76, Lys77, Lys83, Arg119, and Lys120 and acidic residues Glu80, Glu87, and Glu153 from both interacting subunits, burying a larger surface area of ~870 Å2.
source: By contrast, the lateral interface in the new MtbFtsZ structure is composed of basic residues Arg76, Lys77, Lys83, Arg119, and Lys120 and acidic residues Glu80, Glu87, and Glu153 from both interacting subunits, burying a larger surface area of ~870 Å2 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the new MtbFtsZ structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The charged residues involved in both lateral interfaces are generally conserved, indicating that they are functionally relevant.
source: The charged residues involved in both lateral interfaces are generally conserved (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating that they are functionally relevant.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The electrostatic nature of lateral interactions was predicted in earlier studies probing the effects of pH and ionic strength on FtsZ protofilament bundling.
source: Such an electrostatic nature was predicted in earlier studies probing the effects of pH and ionic strength on FtsZ protofilament bundling (Beuria et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In the previous MtbFtsZ structure, only two of the three FtsZ subunits (A and B) in each protofilament participated in lateral interactions.
source: Interestingly, in the previous MtbFtsZ structure (Li et al., 2013), only two of the three FtsZ subunits (A and B) in each protofilament participated in such lateral interactions, whereas the charged residues Arg229 and Asp301 in subunit C were ~6 Å apart (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the previous MtbFtsZ structure.

claim: The in vitro observations suggest the presence of weak lateral interactions between MtbFtsZ protofilaments.
source: These in vitro observations suggest the presence of weak lateral interactions between MtbFtsZ protofilaments, in agreement with earlier electron microscopy studies as well as predictions based on kinetic modeling (Lan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural observations and supported by previous studies.

claim: FtsZ-pBpa variants R78pBpa, N79pBpa, D82pBpa, R85pBpa, R89pBpa, K155pBpa, and S231pBpa produced covalently linked homodimers upon UV irradiation.
source: Upon irradiation with long-wavelength UV light, we found that FtsZ-pBpa variants R78pBpa, N79pBpa, D82pBpa, R85pBpa, R89pBpa, K155pBpa, and S231pBpa produced covalently linked homodimers, as demonstrated by immunoblotting analysis (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Photocrosslinking results demonstrate that both lateral interfaces mediate interactions between FtsZ subunits in living cells.
source: These photocrosslinking results clearly demonstrate that both lateral interfaces mediate interactions between FtsZ subunits in living cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the photocrosslinking experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Random screening identified FtsZ-pBpa variants resulting from insertion of the TAG amber codon at 10 distinct sites, with four variants (R78, D82, R85, K140) forming photocrosslinked FtsZ dimers.
source: We obtained 31 colonies that yielded crosslinked FtsZ products. We then sequenced the ftsZ genes from these 31 colonies and identified FtsZ-pBpa variants resulting from insertion of the TAG amber codon at 10 distinct sites. Our immunoblotting analysis indicated that photocrosslinked FtsZ dimers were formed for four of these ten variants (corresponding to pBpa incorporated at residue positions R78, D82, R85, or K140; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by the random screening results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Residue K140 is located at the protofilament longitudinal interface.
source: Among these four positions, residue K140 is located at the protofilament longitudinal interface and the FtsZK140A mutant was earlier demonstrated to complement an ftsZ conditional-null strain (Li et al., 2013; Matsui et al., 2012), while R78, D82, and R85 are located at lateral interface two observed in our crystal structure.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge and previous studies.

claim: Residues R78, D82, and R85 are located at lateral interface two.
source: Among these four positions, residue K140 is located at the protofilament longitudinal interface and the FtsZK140A mutant was earlier demonstrated to complement an ftsZ conditional-null strain (Li et al., 2013; Matsui et al., 2012), while R78, D82, and R85 are located at lateral interface two observed in our crystal structure.
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure determination.

claim: Random photocrosslinking screening confirms the presence of at least two interfaces involved in FtsZ assembly in living cells, both consistent with crystallographic analyses.
source: Taken together, our photo-crosslinking analyses based on unbiased, random introduction of pBpa confirm the presence of at least two interfaces that are involved in FtsZ assembly in living cells, both consistent with our in vitro crystallographic analyses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the random screening and crystallographic data.

claim: Three pBpa variants (K121pBpa, D122pBpa, and D304pBpa) failed to complement wild-type FtsZ.
source: Our photo-crosslinking analyses were performed for pBpa variants that could complement wild-type FtsZ. We were surprised to find that three variants (K121pBpa and D122pBpa from lateral interface 2, and D304pBpa from lateral interface 1) failed to complement (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by complementation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: K121L and D304L mutations failed to complement in leucine replacement experiments.
source: To exclude potential artifacts introduced by pBpa, we replaced each of the corresponding interfacial residues with hydrophobic leucine and then characterized these mutant proteins using a similar complementation approach (Figure 4, Table 2) (Stricker and Erickson, 2003). As with pBpa replacement, K121L and D304L failed to complement (Figure 4, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by complementation assay data shown in Figure 4 and Table 2.

claim: D122L mutation was sufficient for complementation, unlike D122pBpa.
source: However, unlike D122pBpa, the D122L mutation was sufficient for complementation.
evidence: This is based on complementation assay results.

claim: Purified FtsZK121L and FtsZD304L retained similar GTPase activity to wild-type.
source: However, purified FtsZK121L and FtsZD304L retained similar GTPase activity to that of wildtype (data not shown), and assembled into protofilaments in a GTP-dependent manner, arguing against the possibility of protein misfolding.
evidence: This is based on biochemical assays of the mutant proteins.

claim: FtsZK121L and FtsZD304L assembled into protofilaments in a GTP-dependent manner.
source: However, purified FtsZK121L and FtsZD304L retained similar GTPase activity to that of wildtype (data not shown), and assembled into protofilaments in a GTP-dependent manner, arguing against the possibility of protein misfolding.
evidence: This is based on assembly assays of the mutant proteins.

claim: None of the three non-functional pBpa variants K121pBpa, D122pBpa, and D304pBpa produced any crosslinked dimer.
source: We performed photocrosslinking studies on the non-functional pBpa variants by expressing them in cells that also expressed the AviTagged wild-type FtsZ. Unlike functional pBpa variants (Figure 2), none of the three variants K121pBpa, D122pBpa, and D304pBpa produced any crosslinked dimer (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by photocrosslinking data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The loss of FtsZ function in K121pBpa, D122pBpa, and D304pBpa variants is likely linked to a disruption of lateral interactions.
source: These results indicate that the loss of FtsZ function in these variants is likely linked to a disruption of lateral interactions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the photocrosslinking and complementation data.

claim: Two double mutants across the interface (D304L/S231E and D304L/S231Q) showed complementation, demonstrating the formation of lateral interface one in vivo.
source: To address this possibility, we generated two double mutants across the interface (D304L/S231E and D304L/S231Q) and observed complementation (Figure 5), demonstrating the formation of lateral interface one in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by complementation assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The two lateral interfaces observed in vitro are important for FtsZ function in vivo.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the two lateral interfaces we observed in vitro are important for FtsZ function in vivo, and lack of complementation is likely due to loss of lateral contacts.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and complementation studies.

claim: Lateral interactions are predominantly mediated by van der Waals interactions, which are sensitive to surface geometry.
source: These results, together with those from double mutagenesis (Figure 5), suggest that lateral interactions are predominantly mediated by van der Waals interactions, which are sensitive to surface geometry; the charge complementarity may enhance these associations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mutagenesis results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Charge complementarity may enhance lateral associations between FtsZ protofilaments.
source: These results, together with those from double mutagenesis (Figure 5), suggest that lateral interactions are predominantly mediated by van der Waals interactions, which are sensitive to surface geometry; the charge complementarity may enhance these associations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mutagenesis results.

claim: Lateral interactions between FtsZ protofilaments are much weaker on a per subunit basis compared with hydrophobic longitudinal interactions.
source: Moreover, these results also suggest that lateral interactions between FtsZ protofilaments are much weaker on a per subunit basis in comparison with hydrophobic longitudinal interactions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mutagenesis results.

claim: Protofilament formation is a prerequisite for lateral interactions to occur.
source: This balance prompted us to examine whether protofilament formation is a prerequisite for lateral interactions to occur. To this end, we introduced A181E, a mutation known to disrupt the longitudinal interface (Li et al., 2013), into a set of pBpa variants of FtsZ, including R78pBpa, N79pBpa, D82pBpa, R85pBpa, R89pBpa, K155pBpa, and S231pBpa, all of which produced covalently linked FtsZ dimers upon UV irradiation (Figures 2B and 3B). We then performed in vivo photocrosslinking analysis with this set of A181E-containing pBpa variants, and found that photocrosslinked dimers were no longer detectable for all such variants (Figure 6). Thus, protofilament preassembly is required for lateral interactions to occur, consistent with the hypothesis that the lateral interactions are generally weak on a per-subunit basis.
evidence: This is supported by photocrosslinking data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The intracellular concentration of FtsZ (~5.6 μM) is much higher than the critical concentration (~1 μM).
source: Given that the intracellular concentration (~5.6 μM) (Li et al., 2014) is much higher than the critical concentration (~1 μM) (González et al., 2003), it is reasonable to assume that most FtsZ molecules assemble into protofilaments in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Most FtsZ molecules assemble into protofilaments in vivo.
source: Given that the intracellular concentration (~5.6 μM) (Li et al., 2014) is much higher than the critical concentration (~1 μM) (González et al., 2003), it is reasonable to assume that most FtsZ molecules assemble into protofilaments in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on concentration comparisons from cited studies.

claim: FtsZ mutant proteins D304L and K121L are capable of forming GTP-dependent protofilaments.
source: We first confirmed that these FtsZ mutant proteins (D304L and K121L) are still capable of forming GTP-dependent protofilaments (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: When laterally disruptive FtsZ is co-expressed with wild-type FtsZ, they can stochastically copolymerize to form hybrid protofilaments.
source: This capacity indicates that, when the laterally disruptive FtsZ is co-expressed with wild-type FtsZ, they can stochastically copolymerize to form hybrid protofilaments.
evidence: This is an inference based on the assembly capacity of the mutant proteins.

claim: There exists a critical fraction of laterally disruptive subunits within a protofilament, above which the combined lateral interactions are insufficient to exceed the entropic cost of immobilizing the protofilament.
source: Given that the lateral interactions are weak, we expect that there exists a critical fraction of laterally disruptive subunits within a protofilament, above which the combined lateral interactions are insufficient to exceed the entropic cost of immobilizing the protofilament.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on the weak nature of lateral interactions.

claim: When the cellular proportion of laterally disruptive FtsZ increases, the fraction of such subunits in the Z-ring decreases.
source: As a consequence, when the cellular proportion of laterally disruptive FtsZ increases, the fraction of such subunits in the Z-ring decreases (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by modeling results shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Laterally disruptive mutants K121L and D304L and the laterally nondisruptive mutant R78L were all efficiently incorporated into the Z-ring when the cellular proportions of mutant FtsZ proteins were ~40%.
source: We observed that the laterally disruptive mutants K121L and D304L and the laterally nondisruptive mutant R78L were all efficiently incorporated into the Z-ring (Figure 7C), when the cellular proportions of mutant FtsZ proteins were ~40% (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7C and Western blot data in Figure 7B.

claim: When the cellular proportions of mutant FtsZ increased to ~60%, midcell fluorescence was reduced to virtually undetectable levels for the laterally defective mutants D304L and K121L.
source: The cellular proportions of mutant FtsZ (mNeonGreen tagged and untagged) increased to ~60% (as shown in Figure 7D), while the total levels of mNeonGreen-tagged FtsZ and untagged FtsZ (wild-type and mutant) were expressed at similar levels as before (Figure 7B). Fluorescence imaging demonstrated that midcell fluorescence was reduced to virtually undetectable levels for the laterally defective mutants, D304L and K121L(Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7E and Western blot data in Figure 7D.

claim: Z-rings remained visible in cells expressing a high level of the laterally non-disruptive mutant R78L.
source: By contrast, Z-rings remained visible in cells expressing a high level of the laterally non-disruptive mutant R78L (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Lateral interactions are important for FtsZ protofilament assembly into the Z-ring.
source: Collectively, these results strongly suggest that lateral interactions are important for FtsZ protofilament assembly into the Z-ring.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fluorescence microscopy experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: FtsZ and tubulin share a similar overall structure and use similar longitudinal interfaces to form protofilaments.
source: FtsZ and its eukaryotic counterpart tubulin share a similar overall structure and use similar longitudinal interfaces to form protofilaments.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FtsZ and tubulin.

claim: Unlike tubulin, which exhibits strong lateral interactions to form multi-stranded microtubules, FtsZ polymerizes into single-stranded protofilaments.
source: However, unlike tubulin, which exhibits strong lateral interactions to form multi-stranded microtubules, FtsZ polymerizes into single-stranded protofilaments (Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Romberg et al., 2001), and undergoes GTP hydrolysis-driven treadmilling (Bisson-Filho et al., 2017; Chen and Erickson, 2005; Loose and Mitchison, 2014; Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: FtsZ undergoes GTP hydrolysis-driven treadmilling.
source: However, unlike tubulin, which exhibits strong lateral interactions to form multi-stranded microtubules, FtsZ polymerizes into single-stranded protofilaments (Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Romberg et al., 2001), and undergoes GTP hydrolysis-driven treadmilling (Bisson-Filho et al., 2017; Chen and Erickson, 2005; Loose and Mitchison, 2014; Mukherjee and Lutkenhaus, 1994; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: FtsZ protofilaments coalesce and attach to the membrane at the division site through ZipA and FtsA, forming the Z-ring.
source: These FtsZ protofilaments further coalesce and attach to the membrane at the division site through ZipA and FtsA (Hale and de Boer, 1997; Pichoff and Lutkenhaus, 2002), forming the Z-ring.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Two different lateral interfaces of FtsZ protofilaments were directly observed based on crystallographic analysis.
source: In this study, we directly observed two different lateral interfaces of FtsZ protofilaments based on crystallographic analysis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on crystallographic data.

claim: The presence of lateral interfaces in living cells was confirmed via in vivo photocrosslinking.
source: We subsequently confirmed the presence of these lateral interfaces in living cells via in vivo photocrosslinking.
evidence: This is based on photocrosslinking experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Weak, yet functionally important, lateral interfaces are involved in Z-ring assembly.
source: Finally, we demonstrated that these weak, yet functionally important, lateral interfaces are involved in Z-ring assembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the complementation and fluorescence microscopy experiments.

claim: The antiparallel protofilament arrangement would preclude treadmilling of FtsZ.
source: The antiparallel protofilament arrangement would preclude treadmilling of FtsZ.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the structural arrangement observed.

claim: Transient lateral interactions induce changes in treadmilling velocities of single protofilaments when they collide, rather than mediate the formation of a stable and static higher order architecture.
source: We propose that transient lateral interactions induce changes in treadmilling velocities of single protofilaments when they collide, rather than mediate the formation of a stable and static higher order architecture.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the findings of the study.

claim: The mechanism of FtsZ treadmilling is distinct from that of actin, for which lateral interactions are not directly involved.
source: It is noteworthy that the cooperative assembly of single-stranded FtsZ protofilaments implies that the mechanism of FtsZ treadmilling is distinct from that of actin, for which lateral interactions are not directly involved.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cooperative assembly behavior observed.

claim: The double-stranded MtbFtsZ-GDP protofilaments have a helical pitch of 132.5 Å.
source: The helices have a pitch of 132.5 Å for MtbFtsZ-GDP (C) and 138.3 Å for MtbFtsZ-GTP (D) protofilaments.
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The double-stranded MtbFtsZ-GTP protofilaments have a helical pitch of 138.3 Å.
source: The helices have a pitch of 132.5 Å for MtbFtsZ-GDP (C) and 138.3 Å for MtbFtsZ-GTP (D) protofilaments.
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The inherently weak lateral interactions are unlikely to mediate formation of higher-order protofilament structures such as those observed in vitro.
source: The inherently weak lateral interactions are unlikely to mediate formation of higher-order protofilament structures such as those observed in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on the weak nature of lateral interactions demonstrated in the study.

claim: A recent electron cryotomography study showed a mean interprotofilament spacing of 6.8 nm, slightly too far apart to support tight interactions between FtsZ protofilaments.
source: A recent electron cryotomography study showed a mean interprotofilament spacing of 6.8 nm, slightly too far apart to support tight interactions between FtsZ protofilaments (Szwedziak et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Membrane-targeting FtsZ is sufficient to reconstitute contractile Z-rings in liposomes.
source: Moreover, membrane-targeting FtsZ (either FtsZ and FtsA, or FtsZ alone with the addition of a membrane-targeting sequence) is sufficient to reconstitute contractile Z-rings in liposomes (Osawa et al., 2008; Osawa and Erickson, 2013; Szwedziak et al., 2014), and to display treadmilling behavior and the reorganization of FtsZ protofilaments into dynamic vortices on supported membranes (Loose and Mitchison, 2014; Ramirez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Membrane-targeting FtsZ displays treadmilling behavior and reorganization of FtsZ protofilaments into dynamic vortices on supported membranes.
source: Moreover, membrane-targeting FtsZ (either FtsZ and FtsA, or FtsZ alone with the addition of a membrane-targeting sequence) is sufficient to reconstitute contractile Z-rings in liposomes (Osawa et al., 2008; Osawa and Erickson, 2013; Szwedziak et al., 2014), and to display treadmilling behavior and the reorganization of FtsZ protofilaments into dynamic vortices on supported membranes (Loose and Mitchison, 2014; Ramirez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The MtbFtsZ crystal is in space group P6522 and contains three GDP-MtbFtsZ subunits per asymmetric unit.
source: Crystals are in space group P6522 and contain three GDP-MtbFtsZ subunits per asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data collection and analysis.

claim: The best MtbFtsZ crystal diffracted X-rays to 2.7 Å resolution, with unit-cell dimensions of a = 100.5 Å, c = 138.3 Å.
source: The best crystal diffracted X-rays to 2.7 Å resolution, with unit-cell dimensions of a = 100.5 Å, c = 138.3 Å.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data collection.

claim: The final MtbFtsZ model contains an FtsZ molecule and a GTP molecule.
source: The final model contains an FtsZ molecule and a GTP molecule.
evidence: This is based on the refined crystal structure.

claim: A mutant was considered to complement the ftsZ conditional-null strain when an induction plate produced at least 80% as many colonies as the repression plate.
source: A mutant was considered to complement the ftsZ conditional-null strain when an induction plate produced at least 80% as many colonies as the repression plate.
evidence: This is the criterion used in the complementation assays.

claim: The fraction of laterally disruptive subunits incorporated into protofilaments follows a Binomial distribution with a mean corresponding to the cellular proportion of laterally disruptive FtsZ.
source: We assume that the fraction of laterally disruptive subunits incorporated into protofilaments follows a Binomial distribution with a mean corresponding to the cellular proportion of laterally disruptive FtsZ (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that this fraction will determine the number of effective lateral bonds that could form between protofilaments.
evidence: This is a modeling assumption used in the simulations shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.
